# FingerprintHub — LLM integration guide

> Self-contained brief for an LLM/agent that needs to understand, integrate
> with, or contribute to FingerprintHub. If you read only one file, read this.
> Human-oriented detail lives in README.md and docs/.

## What this is

FingerprintHub is a small, standalone, **multi-tenant** HTTP service that
shares **perceptual-hash (pHash) fingerprints of known-bad scam images** across
multiple Discord bots/servers. One server fingerprints a scam image → every
participating server can recognize it without redoing the manual review.

Stack: Python 3.13+, aiohttp (async HTTP), psycopg 3 (synchronous Postgres
driver, offloaded to a thread pool so it never blocks the event loop), Alembic
migrations, AES-GCM field encryption for sensitive text.

**The hub is deliberately dumb about images.** It only stores and serves the
`phash_hex` string. It NEVER decodes images, computes pHashes, or does Hamming
matching. All of that happens client-side. The hub is a **sync source +
contribution target**, never on a client's moderation hot path.

First consumer is Nexarion (sibling repo at `/home/webhead/VRDiscord/Nexarion`),
but the hub is consumer-agnostic: any bot that can compute a compatible pHash
and speak the HTTP API below can join.

## Mental model in one paragraph

Each client bot keeps its OWN local fingerprint store + in-memory index and
matches messages locally (network-free hot path). In the background it pulls
incremental updates from the hub (`GET /v1/fingerprints/sync`), upserting peer
fingerprints locally and deleting tombstones. When staff mark a new image, the
client writes locally first, then contributes to the hub in the background.
Enforcement "hit" reports are fire-and-forget. So the hub is a **replication
backplane**, not a lookup service you call per-message.

## How to talk to it

- Base URL: wherever the hub is deployed; default bind is `127.0.0.1:58751`
  (`FINGERPRINTHUB_HOST`/`_PORT`). Localhost-only by default — no public network
  exposure. A client runs on the same host (or tunnels in).
- Every endpoint except `GET /v1/health` requires `X-API-Key: fph_…`. The raw
  key is never stored; only its sha256 hash is. Get a key from an operator
  (`tools/create_consumer.py`).
- Scopes are independent flags (NOT hierarchical): `read`, `write`, `admin`.
  Most integrations get `read,write`. `admin` is held in reserve, not issued.
- Error bodies are JSON `{"error": "..."}`; `409` also includes `existing_id`.
- DB outage → `503 {"error": "database temporarily unavailable"}` on any
  endpoint; `/v1/health` then returns `503 {"status": "degraded", "db": false}`.
- Rate-limited per consumer (default 300 req/min → `429`; in-memory sliding
  window, resets on hub restart).

## API reference (all paths under `/v1`)

| Method | Path | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1/health` | none | liveness + DB ping → `{"status":"ok","db":true}` |
| GET | `/v1/fingerprints/sync` | read | incremental pull (the core of integration) |
| POST | `/v1/fingerprints` | write | contribute a fingerprint |
| POST | `/v1/fingerprints/{id}/hit` | write | record enforcement (stats only) |
| POST | `/v1/fingerprints/{id}/flag` | write | flag someone else's row; idempotent; auto-hides at threshold |
| DELETE | `/v1/fingerprints/{id}` | write | soft-delete YOUR OWN row (or admin: any) |
| GET | `/v1/fingerprints/{id}` | read | detail; secrets gated to owner/admin |
| GET | `/v1/fingerprints` | read | browse (filters: category, algorithm, consumer_id, limit, offset) |
| GET | `/v1/fingerprints/stats` | read | aggregates only |

### GET /v1/fingerprints/sync — the endpoint you must implement against

Query params: `since` (last durably-applied `sync_seq`; default `0`), `limit`
(clamped to `[1, 500]`, default `200`), and optional compatibility filter
`algorithm`, `algorithm_version`, `normalization_version`.

Returns rows with `sync_seq > since`, **including hidden/deleted tombstones**,
**excluding the caller's own contributions**. Omits `reason`/`source_url` and
hit stats.

```json
{
  "fingerprints": [
    {"id": 48, "sync_seq": 48, "phash_hex": "0123…", "algorithm": "phash",
     "algorithm_version": "imagehash.phash", "normalization_version": "alpha_white_v1",
     "category": "scam", "action": "timeout", "consumer_id": 2,
     "source_guild_id": null, "added_at_ms": 1782…, "updated_at_ms": 1782…,
     "auto_added": false, "provenance": "manual_staff", "status": "active"}
  ],
  "next_since": 48,
  "has_more": false
}
```

Client contract: apply the page, THEN set your watermark to `next_since` (after,
not before, durably persisting). If `has_more`, immediately request again with
`since=next_since`. For `status` in `{hidden, deleted}`, remove the row locally
(it's a tombstone).

### POST /v1/fingerprints — contribute

```json
{"phash_hex": "0123456789abcdef", "category": "scam", "action": "timeout",
 "algorithm": "phash", "algorithm_version": "imagehash.phash",
 "normalization_version": "alpha_white_v1",
 "source_guild_id": "…", "reason": "…", "source_url": "…",
 "auto_added": false, "provenance": "manual_staff"}
```

- `phash_hex`: required, 16 lowercase hex.
- `category`: required, one of `scam|nsfw|crypto|phishing|other`.
- `action`: required, one of `kick|timeout` (a softban-intent hint; clients may
  honor or override locally).
- The compatibility triple `algorithm/algorithm_version/normalization_version`
  defaults to `phash` / `imagehash.phash` / `alpha_white_v1` — the reference
  recipe under "Computing a compatible pHash" below. Use YOUR triple if your
  preprocessing differs, and filter sync on it.
- `reason`/`source_url` are encrypted at rest and redacted from non-owners.
- `201` → created row (owner sees secrets). `409 {"error":"duplicate…",
  "existing_id":N}` → a live row already exists for this `(phash_hex, consumer)`.
  `400` → invalid input.

### The other endpoints (quick)

- `POST /v1/fingerprints/{id}/hit` — body `{"guild_id":"…","distance":2}` (all
  optional). Bumps `hit_count`/`last_hit_at_ms`; does NOT advance `sync_seq`.
  Returns `{"id":N,"hit_count":M}`; `404` if missing/deleted.
- `POST /v1/fingerprints/{id}/flag` — body `{"reason":"…"}` (optional).
  Idempotent per consumer. Auto-hides the row once
  `FINGERPRINTHUB_AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD` (default 2) DISTINCT consumers flag
  it. Response shows current `flag_count`/`status`/`hidden`.
- `DELETE /v1/fingerprints/{id}` — soft-delete (tombstone). `204` if you own it
  or hold `admin`; `403` if you don't own it (use `/flag` instead); `404` if
  already gone.
- `GET /v1/fingerprints/{id}` — full record; `reason`/`source_url` are `null`
  unless you own the row or hold `admin`; a `hidden` row → `404` for non-owners.
- `GET /v1/fingerprints` — browse; default `limit=50` (max 200);
  `include_hidden` honored only with `admin`.
- `GET /v1/fingerprints/stats` — `total_active/hidden/deleted`, `total_hits`,
  `by_category`, `by_provenance`, `active_consumers`.

## The sync protocol (why it's designed this way)

- **`sync_seq`** is a monotonic value from a Postgres sequence, NOT a timestamp.
  This makes sync immune to clock skew and same-millisecond ordering bugs;
  pages use strict `>` on it.
- **`sync_seq` advances on CONTENT changes only** (insert, resurrect, status
  flips hide/delete). It is NOT touched by stats-only writes (hits,
  sub-threshold flags). So a popular fingerprint that gets hits every minute
  does NOT churn every client's sync feed.
- **Tombstones**: deletes are soft (`status='deleted'`) and hides set
  `status='hidden'`; both get a fresh `sync_seq` so they propagate. Clients
  delete these locally. Physical purge is a deferred retention concern.
- **The feed excludes your own contributions** (`consumer_id <> requester`) —
  so you never re-ingest your own rows. Use ONE key per bot for both sync and
  contribute, or you'll lose this property.
- **Compatibility filter**: pass your triple so you only ingest hashes you can
  actually Hamming-compare against.

## Trust model (cross-consumer, security-relevant dataset)

- You may **hard-delete only your OWN** contributions (→ tombstone).
- You may only **flag** someone else's row. Once enough distinct consumers flag
  it (default 2), it auto-hides (and a hide-tombstone propagates to everyone).
- `admin` scope can delete anything (held in reserve; not issued to any
  consumer yet).
- This means one server's mistake or bad actor can't silently delete protection
  for everyone.

## Computing a compatible pHash (the reference triple, exactly)

The hub never validates hashes — compatibility is a client-side contract, and
an almost-right implementation produces hashes that silently never match
anyone's. Three production consumers (Nexarion, VRDHelper, EmuVR Invites)
interoperate with EXACTLY this recipe (from Nexarion's
`helpers/scam_detection/fingerprint_hash.py`); copy it, don't approximate it:

```python
import io
import imagehash
from PIL import Image

def compute_phash_hex(image_bytes: bytes) -> str:
    with Image.open(io.BytesIO(image_bytes)) as image:
        image.load()                    # animated images: frame 0 only (no seek)
        # alpha_white_v1: flatten transparency onto opaque WHITE.
        # Non-transparent modes pass through UNCHANGED (no forced RGB convert —
        # imagehash grayscales internally).
        if image.mode in ("RGBA", "LA") or (
            image.mode == "P" and "transparency" in image.info
        ):
            rgba = image.convert("RGBA")
            background = Image.new("RGBA", rgba.size, (255, 255, 255, 255))
            image = Image.alpha_composite(background, rgba).convert("RGB")
        phash = int(str(imagehash.phash(image)), 16)  # defaults: hash_size=8 → 64-bit
    return format(phash & ((1 << 64) - 1), "016x")    # 16 lowercase hex, zero-padded
```

- `imagehash.phash` is called with DEFAULT args (`hash_size=8`,
  `highfreq_factor=4`): grayscale → 32×32 → DCT → top-left 8×8 vs median →
  64-bit hash → `"016x"` gives the wire format.
- **Matching is client-side Hamming** (XOR + popcount) over your local index —
  the hub does none. Production tolerance is 5–6 bits; Nexarion clamps to 0–16
  (beyond ~16 bits on 64 you get chance collisions).
- **Pin your imaging libs** (consumers pin `Pillow==12.2.0`,
  `ImageHash==4.3.2`) and verify hash parity against a known image before
  trusting your integration — library-version drift breaks cross-consumer
  matching silently.
- Client-side input hygiene is YOUR job: consumers cap downloads at 8 MiB,
  guard decompression bombs (50M-pixel cap), and only process
  `png/jpeg/webp/gif`.

## The integration pattern (implement this, don't be naive)

**Do NOT call the hub on your moderation hot path.** Keep your existing local
store + in-memory index and treat the hub as a sync source + contribution
target. Matching stays exactly as fast as a local-only implementation and has
no hard dependency on the hub being reachable at startup (load from local DB at
boot).

The minimal viable client is just **sync + contribute + hit** (VRDHelper ships
exactly this; removals reach it via sync tombstones). `/flag` and `DELETE` are
for moderation flows — add them when staff can remove fingerprints locally.
`action` is advisory: existing consumers override it with their own configured
enforcement rather than honoring the contributor's choice.

### Local schema additions on YOUR side

- `hub_fingerprint_id` (nullable) — the hub row id once linked.
- `origin` (`local` | `hub`) — `local` = you contributed it; `hub` = synced
  from a peer. Drives delete-vs-flag behavior.
- a single-row **sync watermark** (`last_sync_seq BIGINT`).
- a **suppression** table keyed by `hub_fingerprint_id` — rows a moderator
  removed locally, so sync won't resurrect them.
- a partial unique index on `hub_fingerprint_id WHERE NOT NULL` for upserts.

### The four flows (pseudocode)

**Sync (background, every ~300s):**
```
watermark = read local watermark
loop:
  GET /v1/fingerprints/sync?since=watermark&limit=200&algorithm=…&…=…
  for row in fingerprints:
     if triple(row) != your triple:            continue   # defensive
     if row.status in (hidden, deleted):       delete local row by hub id; continue
     if hub id in suppressions:                continue
     if row.action/category not in your enums: skip (log)   # poison-pill guard
     upsert local row (origin='hub', hub_fingerprint_id=row.id)
  persist watermark = next_since   # AFTER applying the page
  stop when has_more is false
if anything changed: rebuild in-memory index
```
Isolate per-row failures so one bad row can't break a whole page.

**Contribute (staff marks an image):**
```
insert locally now (origin='local')  -> return LOCAL id to the UI immediately
background:
  POST /v1/fingerprints {phash_hex, category, action, triple, reason?, source_url?, …}
  on 201 -> stamp local row: hub_fingerprint_id = resp.id
  on 409 -> stamp with resp.existing_id   # a prior attempt already landed it
  on error -> leave unlinked; next contribute/backfill reconciles
```

**Remove (staff removes a fingerprint):**
```
delete locally
if origin == 'local' and hub_fingerprint_id:  DELETE /v1/fingerprints/{hub_id}   (fire-and-forget)
if origin == 'hub'  and hub_fingerprint_id:
     add hub_id to local suppression (AWAIT this — must beat the next sync)
     POST /v1/fingerprints/{hub_id}/flag                                       (fire-and-forget)
```

**Hit (after enforcement):**
```
bump local hit_count as before
fire-and-forget POST /v1/fingerprints/{hub_id}/hit   (only if row has a hub id)
```
Schedule fire-and-forget tasks from async code with a running event loop — not
from inside a thread-pool DB call.

### Config knobs (recommended on YOUR side)

Gate behind an enable flag defaulted **OFF**, plus base URL + API key from env,
so you can ship the code + schema migration first (inert), then flip it on:
`hub_enabled` (bool), `hub_base_url`, `hub_sync_interval_seconds` (~300),
`hub_request_timeout_seconds` (~5), and the API key in env. (Nexarion calls
these `image_fingerprint_hub_*` and ALSO requires allowlisting them in
`Nexarion/utils/config_validation/moderation_engine.py` or it crash-loops.)

### One-time backfill

Seed the hub with your existing catalog: read local rows with
`hub_fingerprint_id IS NULL`, `POST` each, stamp the returned id back locally.
Make it idempotent (skip already-linked rows; treat `409` as success via
`existing_id`) so it's safely resumable. No reference script exists yet —
existing consumers only contribute on new adds, so pre-integration rows stay
unlinked until you write this.

### Gotchas (the ones that bite)

- The hub excludes your own contributions from your sync feed — but only if you
  contribute under the SAME key you sync with. One key per bot.
- Advance the watermark to `next_since` AFTER applying the page, not before.
- Suppression on remove of a `hub`-origin row is what stops the next sync from
  resurrecting it (a single flag won't hide it hub-side until the threshold).
- Your pHash preprocessing MUST match the triple you claim, or your hashes
  aren't Hamming-comparable to peers and the whole thing is useless. The
  reference triple is `phash` / `imagehash.phash` / `alpha_white_v1`.
- Re-contributing a `(phash_hex, consumer)` pair resurrects only DELETED rows.
  If YOUR row was auto-HIDDEN by peer flags, contribute returns `409` with its
  id and the row stays hidden — dispute it with an operator, don't retry.

## Data model (for context; you don't write to it directly)

Tables in `alembic/versions/0001_init.py`:

- **`consumers`** — one row per bot. `api_key_hash` = sha256(raw key) (raw key
  never stored). `scopes TEXT[]` ⊆ `{read,write,admin}`. `enabled`.
- **`fingerprints`** — the shared catalog. `phash_hex`; compatibility triple
  `(algorithm, algorithm_version, normalization_version)`; `category` ∈
  {scam,nsfw,crypto,phishing,other}; `action` ∈ {kick,timeout}; `consumer_id`
  (owner); `reason`/`source_url` (encrypted at rest); `status` ∈
  {active,hidden,deleted}; `flag_count`; `sync_seq` (the cursor);
  `hit_count`/`last_hit_at_ms` (stats, never synced). `UNIQUE(phash_hex,
  consumer_id)`.
- **`fingerprint_hits`** — per-hit audit rows (who enforced, where, distance).
- **`fingerprint_flags`** — one row per (fingerprint, flagging consumer); drives
  auto-hide; `UNIQUE(fingerprint_id, consumer_id)` makes flag idempotent.

## Repository layout

```
main.py                      entrypoint: validate Postgres@head -> pool -> create_app -> run
config.py                    flat env-var config (ServiceConfig)
api/app.py                   aiohttp app factory; route table; error + auth middleware
api/auth.py                  X-API-Key -> sha256 lookup -> scope + rate-limit
api/fingerprints.py          HTTP handlers; validation + presentation/redaction
api/fingerprint_store.py     DB CRUD; sync_seq + tombstone invariants live here
api/consumers_store.py       consumer rows + API-key primitives
api/errors.py                handle_errors decorator, parse_json_body
utils/                       postgres_utils, field_encryption, async_utils,
                             config_access, time_utils
alembic/                     schema history (0001_init); forward migrations only
tools/create_consumer.py     operator CLI: mint a consumer + one-time API key
tools/generate_field_key.py  operator CLI: generate an AES-256 field-encryption key
docs/                        API.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLIENT_INTEGRATION.md, OPERATIONS.md
tests/                       Postgres-backed, DESTRUCTIVE (TRUNCATE); skipped unless DSN set
```

## Environment variables (all `FINGERPRINTHUB_`-prefixed)

- `FINGERPRINTHUB_DATABASE_URL` — Postgres DSN (required). Prod points at the
  host's native `postgresql.service`, `127.0.0.1:5432/fingerprinthub`. Local
  dev uses docker-compose Postgres on `:54330`.
- `FINGERPRINTHUB_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` — `keyid:base64(32-byte AES key)`,
  comma-separated; INDEPENDENT from Nexarion's keys (separate blast radius).
- `FINGERPRINTHUB_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_ACTIVE_KEY_ID` — which key id encrypts new
  `reason`/`source_url`. Back up the keys durably and SEPARATELY — losing them
  loses those fields forever.
- `FINGERPRINTHUB_HOST` / `FINGERPRINTHUB_PORT` — bind (default
  `127.0.0.1:58751`).
- Optional knobs (defaults shown): `FINGERPRINTHUB_RATE_LIMIT=300`,
  `FINGERPRINTHUB_AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD=2`, `FINGERPRINTHUB_MAX_SYNC_LIMIT=500`,
  `FINGERPRINTHUB_DEFAULT_SYNC_LIMIT=200`, `FINGERPRINTHUB_MAX_LIST_LIMIT=200`,
  `FINGERPRINTHUB_BLOCKING_IO_MAX_WORKERS=16`, `FINGERPRINTHUB_LOG_LEVEL=INFO`.

`.env.example` is a fill-in-the-blanks template. Secrets live ONLY in `.env`
(chmod 600, gitignored). Never committed.

## Commands

```bash
# ---- bootstrap on a fresh machine (ordered) ----
python3.13 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env                        # then fill in the values below
docker compose up -d                        # dev-only Postgres on :54330
                                            # (prod: native Postgres, own role+db)
venv/bin/python tools/generate_field_key.py --key-id v1   # paste output into .env
venv/bin/alembic upgrade head               # required BEFORE first start
venv/bin/python tools/create_consumer.py --name mybot --scopes read,write
venv/bin/python main.py                     # serve
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:58751/v1/health    # → {"status":"ok","db":true}

# ---- day-to-day ----
# serve (prod: systemd unit FingerprintHub.service on 127.0.0.1:58751)
venv/bin/python main.py

# migrations
venv/bin/alembic upgrade head
venv/bin/alembic revision -m "describe"     # scaffold a FORWARD migration only

# operator CLIs
venv/bin/python tools/generate_field_key.py --key-id v1
venv/bin/python tools/create_consumer.py --name nexarion --scopes read,write

# tests — Postgres-backed and DESTRUCTIVE (TRUNCATE all tables); skipped
# unless the DSN env var is set. Point ONLY at a disposable DB already at head.
FINGERPRINTHUB_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<disposable-db> venv/bin/python -m pytest
```

## Production discipline (this host IS production)

- Runs against the host's **native** `postgresql.service` with its own
  `fingerprinthub` role + database — NOT the `docker-compose.yml` in this repo
  (that's local-dev only, port 54330).
- Runs as systemd unit `FingerprintHub.service` on `127.0.0.1:58751`. Do NOT
  create/enable/start/restart the unit or touch the production DB without
  explicit approval.
- Startup REQUIRES the DB at Alembic head (it validates, does not auto-migrate).
  Add forward migrations; never edit `0001_init.py` once applied.
- Encryption keys are independent from Nexarion's.

## Conventions

- Conventional Commit prefixes, imperative mood (e.g. `fix: return 409 on
  concurrent duplicate contribute`).
- Migrations use raw SQL (`op.execute`) with `IF NOT EXISTS` / `ON CONFLICT DO
  NOTHING`, matching Nexarion's conventions.
- psycopg is synchronous: every DB call in a handler is wrapped in
  `run_blocking_io(...)` (a bounded thread pool) so it never blocks the aiohttp
  event loop.
